eval_instructions: Test against real .NET AgentFramework and Node.js LangChain agent projects. The CLI runner must use no new runtime dependencies beyond what the agent already has (readline for Node.js, built-in adapters for .NET). The scaffolded CLI must reuse the same agent factory as production. Verify that the existing HTTP entry point is NOT modified in a breaking way.

evals.prompt: Add a CLI runner to this agent
evals.description: Full scaffolding on a .NET AgentFramework project
evals.expected_output: The skill detects a .NET AgentFramework project, scaffolds ConsoleCli.cs with a readline REPL loop, adds a --cli mode check to Program.cs, adds a CLI launch profile to launchSettings.json, builds successfully, and tells the user how to start the CLI with dotnet run --cli.
expectations: Phase 1: Agent type is detected as .NET AgentFramework
Phase 1: shared/agent-detection.md heuristics are followed
Phase 2: Existing CLI files are checked before scaffolding
Phase 3: ConsoleCli.cs is created in the project root or alongside Program.cs
Phase 3: ConsoleCli.cs contains a REPL loop using Console.ReadLine()
Phase 3: ConsoleCli.cs creates Activity objects with Type = ActivityTypes.Message
Phase 3: CancellationToken is wired to Console.CancelKeyPress for clean Ctrl+C exit
Phase 3: All scaffolded lines are marked: // A365 CLI — added by add-cli skill
Phase 4: Program.cs is edited to check for --cli arg or RUN_MODE=cli env var
Phase 4: CLI mode calls ConsoleCli.RunAsync and returns before app.Run()
Phase 4: Existing Program.cs HTTP startup code is preserved unchanged
Phase 4: New Program.cs lines are marked: // A365 CLI — added by add-cli skill
Phase 4: A 'CLI' launch profile is added to Properties/launchSettings.json
Phase 5: dotnet build succeeds
Phase 5: User is told: run with dotnet run --cli or dotnet run --launch-profile CLI
Phase 6: Summary lists files created/modified and the run command

evals.prompt: Add a console runner to this agent
evals.description: Full scaffolding on a Node.js LangChain project
evals.expected_output: The skill detects a Node.js LangChain project, scaffolds src/cli.ts using Node.js readline (no extra deps), adds a 'cli' script to package.json, installs ts-node if needed, builds successfully, and tells the user how to start with npm run cli.
expectations: Phase 1: Agent type is detected as Node.js LangChain
Phase 2: Existing cli.ts or cli.js is checked before scaffolding
Phase 3: src/cli.ts is created
Phase 3: cli.ts imports readline from built-in Node.js module (not a third-party package)
Phase 3: cli.ts imports the agent factory from the existing agentApp or equivalent
Phase 3: cli.ts implements a REPL loop calling agent.invoke() or agent.stream()
Phase 3: SIGINT handler is registered for clean Ctrl+C exit
Phase 3: All scaffolded lines are marked: // A365 CLI — added by add-cli skill
Phase 4: 'cli' script is added to package.json scripts (ts-node src/cli.ts)
Phase 4: ts-node is installed as devDependency if not already present
Phase 4: src/index.ts (HTTP entry point) is NOT broken by the changes
Phase 5: npm install and npm run build succeed
Phase 5: User is told: run with npm run cli
Phase 6: Summary lists files created/modified and the run command

evals.prompt: Add cli runner — CLI already exists
evals.description: Idempotency — ConsoleCli.cs or cli.ts already present
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the existing CLI file, skips scaffolding, verifies the run script is present, and reports that the CLI is already configured.
expectations: Phase 2: Existing CLI file is detected (ConsoleCli.cs or cli.ts)
Phase 3: Scaffolding is SKIPPED — existing file is not overwritten
Phase 4: Run script / launch profile is verified — added if missing, skipped if present
Phase 5: Build is still run and validated
Final summary reports that CLI was already present and confirms run command

evals.prompt: Run this agent from the command line
evals.description: Trigger phrase variation — same expected behavior as eval 1 or 2 depending on detected project type
evals.expected_output: Trigger phrase is recognized and the skill runs the full CLI scaffolding flow for the detected project type.
expectations: Trigger phrase 'run this agent from the command line' activates the add-cli skill
Agent type is detected before any scaffolding
Full scaffolding flow completes for the detected type
Build is validated
Run command is communicated to the user

evals.prompt: Add local chat cli to this node agent
evals.description: Node.js project where ts-node is not installed
evals.expected_output: The skill scaffolds cli.ts, installs ts-node as a devDependency, adds the 'cli' script, and verifies the build.
expectations: Phase 4: ts-node is not found in package.json devDependencies
Phase 4: npm install --save-dev ts-node is run
Phase 4: 'cli' script in package.json uses ts-node src/cli.ts
Phase 5: npm install and build succeed
Final summary confirms ts-node was installed and provides npm run cli as the run command
